items.title: 63476_Jimmie Crawford oral history interview
items.q: Joe Turner, piano player, he played bass (inaudible) in the band, and people like that.

ctx.x: What were the requirements for getting in the union in those days?

Well, I don't know what the joining fee was, I've forgotten. But the requirement -- we were union men, but we were unionized in Buffalo, New York. 533, that was the number of that local in Buffalo. But to get in 802, which is the New York musician's union, well, you just had to either quit the band -- that's it, quit the band and join the union. They wouldn't let us in that union unless we had quit the band. I had to quit, because when Uncle Sam reached out for World War II, I went in the army to play drums, not…

of them gone, some of them died, but the remainder, I didn't keep in touch with them, much. Not that I didn't want to, but I was just in my thing. I had to go make a living and a name for Jimmy Crawford. And that's what I did to the best of my ability. I went through hell, man, I went -- and I know I know a lot, and I have a lot of experiences that I witnessed. My memoirs are treasurable. I just -- I'm proud of knowing what I know about travelling from Maine to Florida, New York to California, and halfway around…
